source: Onkelos Num 7:84; Onkelos Num 7:85; Onkelos Num 7:86; Onkelos Num 7:87; Onkelos Num 7:88
claim_en: THE TOTALS BY THE TAUGHT PARSER. 7:84 [12, 12, 12] — and 'from the princes' no number, the 'from' by its points (sitting 1b's homograph at its Naso seat); 7:85 [130, 70, 2400] — 12 × 130 + 12 × 70 = 2,400, the dual 'thousands' before 'and four' read as two thousand (Onkelos writes the two: 'TWO thousand and four hundred'); 7:86 [12, 10, 120] — 'ten, ten' the distributive, 12 × 10 = 120 (the total that decides 7:14's parse); 7:87 [12, 12, 12, 12] = 12 × (1, 1, 1, 1); 7:88 [24, 60, 60, 60] = 12 × 7:17's [2, 5, 5, 5] — every total computed from the ink's numerals by the engine's own parser (cold_run_sequence.ink_numbers, taught at sitting 1b); the shekel the sela throughout.
middah: ink (every total computed by the engine's parser and checked against the twelve blocks' arithmetic)

check.note: 'thousands' — the dual read as two thousand, 2,400

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 53:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 57:1; Onkelos Num 7:84; Onkelos Num 7:85; Onkelos Num 7:86; Onkelos Num 7:87; Onkelos Num 7:88
claim_en: ON THE DAY OF ITS ANOINTING / AFTER ITS ANOINTING — THE SAME DAY; THE PRIESTS' GIFTS ACQUIRED AT THE ANOINTING; UNITED IN MERIT. 7:84's 'on the day it was anointed' against 7:88's 'after it was anointed' (computed): not long after — the same day, after the anointing; LEVITICUS 7:35-36's PARALLEL — the priests' gifts 'on the day he anointed them': commanded at Sinai, ACQUIRED when anointed (row 53:1); 'by the princes of Israel' — united in counsel, united in merit; 'twelve silver dishes' — the very ones donated, none become unfit; all valid as peace offerings; each credited with twenty-four and sixty (row 57:1 — the export's row omits the sixty he-goats the ink counts; the shelf's, not ours). Onkelos 'after they anointed it'.
middah: plain (the two formulas computed on the ink; the Sifrei's reconciliation and its Leviticus parallel read as they stand)

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 54:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 55:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 56:1; Onkelos Num 7:85; Onkelos Num 7:86; Onkelos Num 7:87
claim_en: TEMPLE VESSELS WEIGH THE SAME SINGLY AND TOGETHER; GOLD WEIGHED IN SILVER — THE 120 DECIDES; EACH CREDITED WITH ALL TWELVE. 'A hundred and thirty each dish' again — the dish by the sanctuary shekel from the total 'two thousand four hundred by the shekel of the sanctuary'; and TEMPLE VESSELS ARE NOT COMMON VESSELS: common ones weighed singly then together gain or lose, these neither — R. Nathan: melted, recast, no change — a data row on the sanctuary's weights (row 54:1); 'twelve golden pans... ten, ten' — 7:14's 'ten gold' is of gold with its weight in silver, decided by 'all the gold of the pans, a hundred and twenty' (row 55:1 — the same total that decides the accents' one-and-ten against eleven); the same pans, none unfit; and it is accounted to EACH prince as if he offered twelve dishes, twelve basins, twelve pans, twelve of every animal (rows 55:1-56:1).
middah: plain (the Sifrei's rows read as they stand; the weights' arithmetic computed on the ink)

check.note: 'ten' — the second of 'ten, ten', the distributive

claim_en: THE VOICE SPEAKING ITSELF — BY THE POINTS; THE TRANSLATION READS BOTH VERBS REFLEXIVELY. 'He heard the Voice speaking to him' — the participle is the REFLEXIVE stem with its tav swallowed (a hiriq under the mem, the doubling dot in the dalet) at 8 Tanakh seats (Num 7:89, Exod 34:33, Ezek 2:2, 43:6 among them) against 'speaking' (the active) at 26 and 'wilderness' at 45 — one consonantal word, three words by the points (computed on the DB's own marks; sitting 1b's law at a verb); the closing 'and He spoke to him' is the DB's plain narrative-past, the active stem (computed); ONKELOS: 'and WHENEVER Moses entered... he heard the voice SPEAKING ITSELF with him... and it was speaking itself with him' — the entry habitual, and BOTH verbs the Voice's self-speech, the reflexive a second time where the Hebrew has the active (cut from the shelf's bytes).
middah: ink (the three pointings of one consonantal word counted on the DB; the two renderings cut from the shelf)

claim_en: TWO VERSES CONTRADICT UNTIL A THIRD RECONCILES — THE THIRTEENTH RULE STATED HERE; THIRTEEN UTTERANCES, THIRTEEN EXCLUSIONS OF AARON. Lev 1:1 'from the tent of meeting' against Exod 25:22 'from above the ark-cover': 'THIS IS A RULE IN THE TORAH: two verses which contradict each other remain in their place until a third comes and reconciles them' — 7:89 is the third: Moses would enter and stand in the tent, the Voice would descend from the heaven of heavens to between the two cherubim ('from between the two cherubim' — Exod 25:22's phrase, its two seats computed), and he heard it from within — Rabbi Ishmael's thirteenth rule in the Sifrei's own words on this verse; R. YEHUDAH B. BETEIRA: THIRTEEN UTTERANCES to Moses and Aaron and thirteen EXCLUSIONS — to Moses alone, to tell Aaron (Exod 25:22 ×3, 30:6 ×2, 31:18, Lev 7:38, Num 7:89 ×3, Lev 1:1, Exod 6:28, Num 3:1) — a count of exclusion-formulas the compile can enumerate against the corpus's frame census (row 58:1).
middah: I13 (two verses reconciled by a third — stated by the Sifrei on 7:89 itself; the thirteen exclusions recorded as an enumerable count)

check.note: 'the cherubim' — the third verse's shared phrase

claim_en: THE VOICE — GREAT, NOT LOW; THE STILL SMALL VOICE RECONCILED TWO WAYS. 'He heard THE Voice' — not a low voice: 'the voice' explicated elsewhere, Deut 5:19's 'a great voice' and Exod 19:16's thunders; against 1 Kgs 19:12's 'a voice, silent, thin': R. Yoshiyah — when He speaks all are silent (Isa 23:2; Lev 10:3 'and Aaron was silent'); R. Yonathan — He with a great voice, the angels low (Isa 62:6-7) — a DISPUTE on the reconciliation, both recorded (row 58:2; the exam's Yoma 4b — the voice cut off at the door).
middah: plain (the dispute recorded as a dispute; the Voice's volume a parameter of the frames)
